newsitem.title: USA: Reebok sees margin pressure rest of year.
newsitem.headline: Reebok sees margin pressure rest of year.

text.p: Reebok International Ltd Chief Financial Officer Kenneth Watchmaker said Thursday he expects the company's gross margins to come under pressure during the second half of this year, but rise the second half of 1998.

"We'll see margin pressure that I expect to be substantial in the third quarter in particular," Watchmaker told analysts and reporters on a conference call. "We could see margins dropping even from where they are right now. I would expect to see margins start to improve in the second half of 1998."
Reebok reported gross margins of 38.5 percent in the second quarter against 38.2 percent last year.

Watchmaker said continuing investments in Reebok's new athletic footwear products incorporating new "technology" accounts will pressure margins in the second half of this year and perhaps into the first half of next year.

However, the new products should eventually post better margins, he said. When asked if the new technology products would help raise gross raise margins to around 40 percent of sales as in years past, Watchmaker replied: "There's no reason the new technology won't deliver historical margins."

A strong shift in sales to the company's new technology footwear, such as its DMX air transfer shoes, helped push average selling prices up in the U.S. for the first time in three years, Watchmaker said.
"For the first time since 1994, we actually saw a small uptick in our average selling price," he said.
The company's strategy of shifting sales in the U.S. to athletic specialty retailers has done well and is ahead of schedule, he said.

Sales to athletic speciality accounts in the U.S. rose by 34 percent and represented 31 percent of the U.S. footwear business, up from 22 percent of sales in last year's second quarter. Conversely, sales to volume retailers fell sharply in the quarter, he said.
